plan.title: --root with a lowercase drive letter is rejected as not the Git working-tree root on Windows

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan group G-I (story id ovpr-g-small-fixes): units P5-U1a + P5-U3a + P5-U3b in one PR. (1) P5-U1a, launcher output: `--root` with a lowercase Windows drive letter is refused (#6005); 'Review and commit' drops most created paths (#6006); `directive upgrade` creates `{ "private": true }` package.json silently on a no-manifest convert (#5965). (2) P5-U3a: the npm-publish post-publish two-pass fixture crashes with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND @deftai/directive-types after every good publish (#5603); fix by bundling the runner with esbuild. (3) P5-U3b: `task materialize:runtime` fails under Git Bash tar, leaves an unrunnable runtime on pnpm checkouts, and does not fail closed (#6220).
narratives.Overview:
## Summary
`--root` with a lowercase drive letter is rejected as not being the Git root.

## Actual
`directive doctor --root "e:\installer-lab\fixtures\g9-concurrent"` → exit 2 `--root must be the Git working-tree root (E:\installer-lab\fixtures\g9-concurrent); got e:\installer-lab\fixtures\g9-concurrent.` The same path with `E:` works.

## Root cause
- Cause: `discoverProject` compares `realpathOrResolve(git toplevel)` with `realpathOrResolve(--root)` by exact string. `realpathSync` (not `.native`) keeps the caller's drive-letter case on Windows.
- Evidence: `packages/cli/src/discover.ts` (rootFlag branch, `toplevel !== rootFlag`).
- Confidence: confirmed.
- Checked: lowercase vs uppercase drive letter.

## Environment
- Directive 0.127.0 (`@deftai/directive` launcher + `@deftai/directive-runtime`), `latest` dist-tag
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Node 24.20.0, npm 11.19.0, pnpm 10.33.2, Git for Windows (system gitconfig `core.autocrlf=true`)
- Shells: Git Bash, PowerShell 7, cmd.exe. Isolated npm prefix/cache; registry = local Verdaccio proxying npmjs. Throwaway fixture repos.
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive user and maintainer, I want the launcher's own output to be correct (Windows root case, a complete commit list, an upgrade that says it creates package.json), the release run to end green after a good publish, and materialize:runtime to work on Windows and pnpm or restore the pin, so that I can trust what Directive tells me and no red run or broken runtime needs a person to explain it.
narratives.StoryId: ovpr-g-small-fixes (carried in the file name so the ordered plan can match it; plan.id stays the id minted from the issue, because the brief tools refuse a different plan.id)
narratives.UnitSpec: ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/units/P5-U1a-launcher-output-edge-cases.md, P5-U3a-release-run-red-after-good-publish.md and P5-U3b-materialize-runtime-windows.md (read all three in full; an 'Update' banner wins over the text below it). Group G-I in scratchpad groups.md; polfer decision D-037 (go wide: one PR for this group, no 5-production-file cap, no guard-only tests).
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
P5-U1a (launcher output):
1. packages/cli/src/discover.ts: add pure `sameRootPath(a, b, platform)` (win32: case-insensitive after separator normalising; elsewhere exact); use it at the `toplevel !== rootFlag` check; on success return git's `toplevel` spelling as `root`.
2. packages/cli/src/plan-present.ts: `collectReviewPaths` builds the complete list from created/modified/migrated/archived; keep the four headline files first; group a folder with more than a few files into one line such as `.agents/skills/ (12 files)`; never list `node_modules/**` or `.deft/directive/wiring-ready.*.json`; drop the `slice(0, 16)` cap. Install, repair and upgrade success all use it.
3. plan-present.ts + bookends.ts: add `willCreatePkg` to `UpgradePlanFields`, set when `convertViaRemovals` and no package.json; `presentUpgradePlan` prints the plain-language bullet and the `-v` line `manifest: create package.json { "private": true }`; after `ensurePackageJson` on the upgrade path print `Created package.json { "private": true }`.
P5-U3a (release run):
4. New packages/core/scripts/bundle-post-publish-runner.mjs: esbuild bundle of packages/core/dist/release-e2e/npm-ops.js (platform node, format esm, all deps bundled) to post-publish-runner/npm-ops.mjs.
5. .github/workflows/npm-publish.yml: `prepare` runs the bundle after the build and uploads that one file as `post-publish-runner-<version>`; `post-publish` downloads it and runs `node post-publish-runner/npm-ops.mjs --post-publish-two-pass "$VERSION"`. Keep no checkout and no pnpm install in post-publish. Fallback (only if bundling fails; say why in the PR): ship built packages/types under node_modules/@deftai/.
6. Touch npm-ops.ts only if it needs a bundle-friendly guard.
P5-U3b (materialize):
7. tasks/materialize.cjs: run tar with cwd = dirname(tgz) and the bare archive name (prefer %SystemRoot%\System32\tar.exe on win32 when present); inject spawnSync for tests.
8. On a pnpm symlinked pin, swap at realpathSync(pinDir) by renaming whole folders, leave the symlink; keep the isCheckoutOwnedDir refusal; npm real folder unchanged.
9. Fail closed: after the swap and before deleting the backup, smoke-check `node <pin>/dist/bin.js --version` and require.resolve of each declared dependency from the pin real path; on failure restore the backup, remove any overlay record, exit non-zero with 'materialize failed; the published pin was restored' (name the missing dependency). Write the overlay record only after the check passes.
10. One changelog fragment changelog.d/6005-launcher-output-and-release-fixes.md (Fixed) naming #6005, #6006, #5965, #5603, #6220.
narratives.Constraint:
- P5-U1a changes output only: do not change which files install, repair or upgrade write; no tool-local cache or runtime outside node_modules (#5965 ask rejected, OVPR rules 1-3); no .gitignore lines (AC13.3); do not touch RECOVERY_GUIDANCE (G-G / P4-U3b owns it).
- P5-U3a: never make the job warn-only or continue-on-error (polfer FINAL on #5603); no checkout or pnpm install in post-publish (CodeQL cache-poisoning rule); do not touch publish/provenance steps or prepare's packing of the two public packages; do not edit content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md or Taskfile.yml release tasks (P3-U1). Tell Scott before merging (release CI).
- P5-U3b: no package.json/lockfile changes; do not touch the cut-context guard (#5910) or the overlay fail-closed rule in install-health/cheap.ts; never write inside pnpm store files in place (rename whole folders only); tip code never runs by default.
- No guard-only 'prevent it coming back' tests (D-037); real behaviour tests only.
- OVPR change gate: read ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/OVPR-CHANGE-GATE.md. Do not edit docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/ and do not ship behaviour that departs from the written OVPR requirements or architecture; stop that part and hand back a change proposal.
- Changelog: add the changelog.d fragment named in file_scope; never edit CHANGELOG.md.
narratives.Dependencies: Depends on: G-F (ovpr-g-doctor, P3-U2: doctor stops writing doctor-state.json, the dirty-tree half of #6006) and G-G (ovpr-g-message-table, P4-U3b: also edits packages/cli/src/bookends.ts). Rebase late; land after both. P5-U3a and P5-U3b have no code dependency. Blocks: none.
narratives.PlanningOrder: design-critique: not warranted, because the OVPR fix plan and its unit specs already decide the design (polfer decisions D-001, D-008, D-037)
narratives.Traces: Closes #6005, #6006, #5965, #5603 (after a green tag run), #6220 (after the Windows live check). Ticket close-outs need polfer's OK.

items.title: On Windows, `--root` with a different drive-letter case than git's toplevel is accepted, and the resolved root equals git's toplevel.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a Windows checkout whose git toplevel is `E:\repo`, when `directive doctor --root "e:\repo"` runs (or `sameRootPath("e:\\x", "E:\\x", "win32")` is called), then the root is accepted and the resolved root equals git's toplevel spelling.

items.title: On Linux and macOS, root comparison is unchanged (exact).

narrative.Acceptance: Given a non-Windows platform, when `sameRootPath("/a/X", "/a/x", "linux")` is called, then it returns false and a mismatched `--root` is still refused.

items.title: After `directive install` on a fresh repo, every created or modified path in the setup summary appears in 'Review and commit', directly or under a grouped folder line.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a setup summary with `.agents/skills/**`, `.githooks/*`, `.github/*`, `xbrief/*` and `.claude/deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs`, when the install success output is presented, then 'Review and commit' lists every one of them, directly or as a grouped folder line, with the four headline files first.

items.title: 'Review and commit' never lists `node_modules` content or wiring-ready readiness markers.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a setup summary that includes `node_modules/**` and `.deft/directive/wiring-ready.<v>.json`, when the review list is built, then neither appears.

items.title: Repair and upgrade success use the same complete list.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a repair or upgrade success summary with created and modified paths, when the success output is presented, then 'Review and commit' is built by the same complete, grouped list.

items.title: `directive upgrade` on a supported old layout with no `package.json` says in the plan, in plain words, that it will create a minimal `package.json`, and after the run prints `Created package.json { "private": true }`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a supported old layout with no `package.json`, when `directive upgrade` shows its plan and then runs, then the plan has a plain-language bullet about creating a minimal package.json (and the `-v` line `manifest: create package.json { "private": true }`), and the output prints `Created package.json { "private": true }`.

items.title: The install plan and output for the no-manifest case are unchanged.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a project with no package.json, when `directive install` shows its plan and runs, then the plan and output text are the same as before this change.

items.title: The bundled post-publish runner starts in a folder with no `node_modules` and gets past module loading.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the output of packages/core/scripts/bundle-post-publish-runner.mjs copied to an empty temp folder with no node_modules, when `node npm-ops.mjs --post-publish-two-pass 0.0.0-test` runs with the registry unreachable, then it fails on the registry, not with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

items.title: On the next release tag (or a `workflow_dispatch` re-run of an existing tag), all npm-publish.yml jobs that run end `success`, including 'Post-publish two-pass fixture'.

narrative.Acceptance: Given this change merged, when npm-publish.yml runs for a release tag or a workflow_dispatch re-run, then every job that runs, including 'Post-publish two-pass fixture', concludes `success` (checked after merge; a further small fix PR is expected if pass 2 then finds a real problem).

items.title: The `post-publish` job still does no checkout and no `pnpm install`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given .github/workflows/npm-publish.yml after the change, when the `post-publish` job steps are read, then there is no actions/checkout step and no pnpm install.

items.title: On Windows, from Git Bash, PowerShell and cmd, `task materialize:runtime` extracts without the 'Cannot connect to C:' error.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an injected spawnSync, when materialize extracts the tarball, then tar is called with cwd = dirname(tgz) and the bare archive file name; and given a Windows pnpm checkout (live check by polfer or Scott), when `task materialize:runtime` runs from Git Bash, PowerShell and cmd, then extraction succeeds.

items.title: On a pnpm checkout, after `task materialize:runtime`, a command that loads a vendored module with a third-party dependency runs with no ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a pnpm-style symlinked pin in a temp tree, when materialize swaps the runtime, then the swap happens at the symlink's real path, the symlink is untouched, and the new runtime resolves its declared dependencies (for example parse5).

items.title: If the materialized runtime can't start, the command exits non-zero, the previous pin works, and no overlay record is left.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a smoke check that fails after the swap, when materialize runs, then it exits non-zero with 'materialize failed; the published pin was restored', the previous pin folder is back in place, and no `.deft-scratch/materialize-runtime-overlay.json` exists.

x-directive/disposition.reason: Smoke check (materialized runtime under Git Bash) is the open #6220 live check

items.title: An npm checkout behaves as before.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an npm-style real-folder pin with hoisted dependencies, when materialize runs, then it swaps the folder as before and the existing materialize tests pass.

### Duplicate / uniqueness triage (2026-10-28)

**Verdict: UNIQUE — keep open.**

Not in the sealed install-ovpr-problem-ledger-2026-10-23 Problems 1–33 ticket map.

No open ticket found for Windows `--root` drive-letter case mismatch in `discoverProject`. Keep as a small CLI discover fix.
